definitions.explanation: Describes something that is disorganized, jumbled, or in complete disorder.
Describes something that has been crushed or mixed into a messy state.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
⟦カバン→カバン：00637_kaban⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中身|なかみ}→中身：01483_nakami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The contents of my bag got all jumbled up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{引|ひ}き{出|だ}し→引き出し：01498_hikidashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{見|み}つからない→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: The inside of the drawer is such a mess that I can't find anything.

examples.japanese: ⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{潰|つぶ}れた→潰れる：04249_tsubureru⟧。
examples.english: The cake got squashed into a mess.
The road turned into a muddy mess from the rain.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}ども→子ども：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べ{物|もの}→食べ物：02890_tabemono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいる→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: The child is playing with their food, making a mess of it.

notes:
ぐちゃぐちゃ is a ⟦{擬態語|ぎたいご}→擬態語：22468_gitaigo⟧ (mimetic word) describing two kinds of messiness: (1) disorganized or chaotic state, and (2) mushy or squashed physical state.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become messy/mushy
- ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make a mess of
- ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧〜: messy ~ (noun modifier)
- ぐちゃぐちゃ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{混|ま}ぜる→混ぜる：02423_mazeru⟧: to mix into a mess

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦めちゃくちゃ→めちゃくちゃ：05178_mechakucha⟧: destroyed, ruined (more extreme; can also mean "absurd")
- ⟦ばらばら→ばらばら：05165_barabara⟧: scattered, disjointed (pieces separated, not necessarily messy)
- ⟦ぐしゃぐしゃ→ぐしゃぐしゃ：noentry⟧: crumpled, wrinkled (closer to crushed paper or fabric)
- ⟦ごちゃごちゃ→ごちゃごちゃ：09369_gochagocha⟧: cluttered, jumbled (focuses on visual disorder)

REGISTER:
Informal and expressive. Common in spoken Japanese and casual writing.
